## Filtering Console Noise

The Supabase Edge Runtime can produce verbose output during local development. The cron checks worker health every second, but sends HTTP only when no healthy worker or current pending startup exists. To get cleaner logs that focus on your worker output, pipe through grep:

```bash frame="none"
npx supabase functions serve --no-verify-jwt 2>&1 | \
  grep -Pv 'serving the request with supabase/functions/[a-zA-Z0-9-]+-worker|^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}T[\d:.]+Z\s*$'
```

This filters out:
- Request serving messages for worker functions
- Empty timestamp lines

:::note[Shell Alias]
Add this to `~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`, then run `source ~/.bashrc` to reload:

```bash frame="none"
alias supabase-serve="npx supabase functions serve --no-verify-jwt 2>&1 | grep -Pv 'serving the request with supabase/functions/[a-zA-Z0-9-]+-worker|^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}T[\d:.]+Z\s*$'"
```

Then just run: `supabase-serve`
:::

## Auto-Restart Behavior

During local development, pgflow automatically:
- Starts workers after a code reload once the previous worker stops or its heartbeat becomes stale
- Recompiles flows when the shape changes
- Checks worker health via cron every second, with one pending startup per function

See [Worker Lifecycle](/concepts/worker-lifecycle/) for details on how this works.

## Initial Worker Registration

The first time you start a worker, you need to trigger it once:

```bash frame="none"
curl http://localhost:54321/functions/v1/my-worker
```

After this initial registration, pgflow's cron keeps the worker running automatically. Local startup uses the same [pending invocation handshake](/deploy/worker-management/#startup-handshake) as production. A lost request can delay retry for up to 60 seconds, plus the cron interval and any remaining debounce. An HTTP 409 while another startup is pending does not authorize another worker.
